To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a Na+/ Mg2+ exchanger exists in the plasma membrane of ovine ruminal (epithelial) cells, which is a key pathway for Mg2+ excretion.
a Na+/ Mg2+ exchanger exists in the cell membrane that is the main pathway for Mg2+ effusion.
a Na+/ Mg2+ exchanger in the apical membrane of ovine ruminal cells is responsible for most of the Mg2+-efflux and that the Mg2+ transport is stimulated by PGE2 and cAMP.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the first demonstration of a Na+-dependent Mg(2+) transport in the epithelial cells of the rumen.
the characterization of a Na+-dependent Mg(2+)-transport system in ovine ruminal mucosal epithelial cells.
a Na+/MgL exchanger that is similar to the Na+/MgL exchanger described for the red blood cell and is involved in cellular Mg2+ extrusions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Na+/Mg(2+)-dependent Mg2+ effux is an essential mechanism for the maintenance of [Mg2]i homeostasis in REC.
the Na+/Mg(2+)-exchanger in the cell membrane is responsible for the Mg2+-efflux from the ruminal epithelial cell and is a potential target for the action of cAMP.
the Na+/Mg(2+)-exchanger is a major Mg(2+)-transport pathway in the cell membranes of ruminal epithelial cell.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Mg2+ effux is mainly mediated by a specific Na+/Mg(2+), K(+)-dependent exchanger.

Mg2+ effusion in the sheep ruminal epithelium is mainly mediated by a Na+/M2+ exchanger, and its activity is regulated by the intracellular cGMP concentration and the intracellular cationic composition.

The main takeaway from our work is that
Mg2+ transport across ruminal epithelium is mediated by a Na+-coupled exchanger.
Mg2+ effusion is a Na(+)-dependent process and the main pathway for Mg2+ effluence is a Na(+)/Mg(2+) exchanger.
